title: Urban water quality concerning anthropogenic pressures and eco‐protective infrastructure in Shymkent, Kazakhstan
content:
Abstract

Anthropogenic pressure poses severe threats to urban water safety in rapidly expanding industrial centers. This study evaluates the spatial and seasonal variations in water quality across Shymkent (South Kazakhstan) during 2023–2024 and assesses the post-implementation efficiency of eco-protective biogas treatment infrastructure. A systematic sampling campaign was conducted across eight seasonal time points (n = 96 total samples), capturing industrial zones, residential areas, and districts equipped with biogas digestion systems. Physicochemical, chemical, heavy metal, and microbiological parameters were quantified using standard spectrophotometric, atomic absorption (AAS), gas chromatographic (GC–MS), and membrane filtration protocols. Interannual (Mann–Whitney U), seasonal (One-Way RM-ANOVA), and spatial (One-Way ANOVA with Tukey HSD, PCA, regression) dynamics were evaluated. Interannual comparisons between 2023 and 2024 revealed significant subtle increases in electrical conductivity (450 ± 35 to 470 ± 30 μS/cm, p = 0.016), ammonium (0.38 ± 0.12 to 0.49 ± 0.15 mg/L, p = 0.004), BOD5 (p = 0.012), and COD (p = 0.024). Spatial analysis demonstrated severe pollution centered in industrial catchments, where nitrites (0.30 ± 0.07 mg/L), electrical conductivity (480 ± 33 μS/cm), and petroleum hydrocarbons (0.08 ± 0.03 mg/L) peaked. Conversely, districts serviced by biogas infrastructure (installed 2017–2022) exhibited significantly suppressed nitrite levels (0.20 ± 0.05 mg/L, Tukey p = 0.018) and coliform counts (5 ± 2 CFU/100 mL, p = 0.002). PCA confirmed that anthropogenic organic variance dropped from 78.4% in industrial zones to 55.2% in biogas-serviced districts.
